text: Trainers' frauds against their own horses
why: Holmes says in ¶220 that trainers have made money by laying against their own horses and stopping them by fraud.

text: Cases before now, when trainers laid against their own horses and stopped them by fraud
why: Holmes refers in ¶220 to 'cases before now' in which trainers did this.

text: Had Straker laid money against his own horse?
why: Holmes raises this as the likely dishonest purpose behind Straker taking out the horse, which makes it a natural question.

text: Had Straker laid money against his own horse? — yes, through agents
why: Laying against one's own horse 'through agents' is the method Holmes himself names in ¶220.

text: Had Straker laid money against his own horse? — no: someone else paid him to stop the horse
